text:
A sphere of mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m is rolling with an initial speed of $1 ms^{-1}$ goes up an inclined plane which makes an angle of 30${}^{\circ }$ with the horizontal plane, without slipping. How long will the sphere take to return to the starting point A?


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a solid sphere $I=\dfrac{2}{5}mR^{2}$. Rolling without slipping on an incline of angle $θ=30^{\circ }$, the acceleration of the centre is

$a=\dfrac{g\sin θ}{1+\dfrac{I}{mR^{2}}}=\dfrac{9.8\times \frac{1}{2}}{1+\frac{2}{5}}=3.5\text{m s}^{-2}$

directed down the incline. Static friction acts up the incline both on the way up (it slows the spin) and on the way down (it speeds up the spin), so the same $a$ applies throughout.

Going up, the sphere stops after $0=1-3.5t_{1}\Rightarrow t_{1}=\dfrac{1}{3.5}\text{s}$.

Under the same constant acceleration it covers the same distance back to A in the same time, so

$T=2t_{1}=\dfrac{2}{3.5}\approx 0.57\text{s}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift

text: The velocity of a particle is $v = v_{0} + gt + Ft^{2}$. Its position is x = 0 at t = 0; then its displacement after time (t = 1) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The velocity of a particle is given by $v=v_{0}+gt+Ft^{2}$. Its position is $x=0$ at $t=0$. To find its displacement after time $t=1$, follow these steps:

Given:

$v=v_{0}+gt+Ft^{2}$

We know that:

$\frac{dx}{dt}=v_{0}+gt+Ft^{2}$

To find the displacement, integrate both sides with respect to $t$:

$\int\limits _{x=0}^{x}dx=\int\limits _{t=0}^{t=1}(v_{0}+gt+Ft^{2})dt$

This simplifies to:

$x=\left [v_{0}t+\frac{gt^{2}}{2}+\frac{Ft^{3}}{3}\right ]_{t=0}^{t=1}$

Evaluating the integral from $t=0$ to $t=1$:

$x=v_{0}+\frac{g}{2}+\frac{F}{3}$

Therefore, the displacement after time $t=1$ is:

$x=v_{0}+\frac{g}{2}+\frac{F}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift

text: A rubber ball is released from a height of 5 m above the floor. It bounces back repeatedly, always rising to $\frac{81}{100}$ of the height through which it falls. Find the average speed of the ball. (Take $g = 10 ms^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each bounce takes the ball to $\dfrac{81}{100}$ of the height it fell from. Since height $\propto v^{2}$, the speed just after a bounce is $e=\sqrt{0.81}=0.9$ times the speed just before it.


[IMG]

Distance: the ball falls $h=5\text{m}$ once, then travels up and down each height $e^{2}h,e^{4}h,\ldots$ twice:

$d=h+2h\left (e^{2}+e^{4}+\ldots \right )=h\left (1+\dfrac{2e^{2}}{1-e^{2}}\right )=h\dfrac{1+e^{2}}{1-e^{2}}=5\times \dfrac{1.81}{0.19}=47.6\text{m}$

Time: the first fall takes $T=\sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{2\times 5}{10}}=1\text{s}$. After the $n$th bounce the ball leaves with $e^{n}$ times the first impact speed, so its up-and-down trip takes $2e^{n}T$:

$t=T+2T\left (e+e^{2}+\ldots \right )=T\left (1+\dfrac{2e}{1-e}\right )=T\dfrac{1+e}{1-e}=1\times \dfrac{1.9}{0.1}=19\text{s}$

Average speed:

$v_{\text{avg}}=\dfrac{d}{t}=\dfrac{47.6}{19}\approx 2.50\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift

text:
The four arms of a Wheatstone bridge have resistances as shown in the figure. A galvanometer of 15$\Omega$ resistance is connected across BD. Calculate the current through the galvanometer when a potential difference of 10V is maintained across AC.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Take $V_{C}=0$, so $V_{A}=10\text{V}$; the galvanometer of resistance $15\Omega$ joins B and D.

KCL at B (sum of currents leaving B is zero), multiplied by 300:

$\dfrac{V_{B}-10}{100}+\dfrac{V_{B}-V_{D}}{15}+\dfrac{V_{B}}{10}=0\Rightarrow 3(V_{B}-10)+20(V_{B}-V_{D})+30V_{B}=0$

$53V_{B}-20V_{D}=30\text{(i)}$

KCL at D, multiplied by 60:

$\dfrac{V_{D}-10}{60}+\dfrac{V_{D}-V_{B}}{15}+\dfrac{V_{D}}{5}=0\Rightarrow (V_{D}-10)+4(V_{D}-V_{B})+12V_{D}=0$

$-4V_{B}+17V_{D}=10\text{(ii)}$

From (ii), $V_{D}=\dfrac{10+4V_{B}}{17}$; substituting in (i) gives $901V_{B}-200-80V_{B}=510$, so

$V_{B}=\dfrac{710}{821}\text{V},V_{D}=\dfrac{10+4\times \frac{710}{821}}{17}=\dfrac{650}{821}\text{V}$

The current through the galvanometer is

$I_{G}=\dfrac{V_{B}-V_{D}}{15}=\dfrac{60}{821\times 15}=\dfrac{4}{821}\text{A}\approx 4.87\times 10^{-3}\text{A}=4.87\text{mA}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Two identical blocks A and B each of mass m resting on the smooth horizontal floor are connected by a light spring of natural length L and spring constant K. A third block C of mass m moving with a speed v along the line joining A and B collides with A. The maximum compression in the spring is

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


From conservation of momentum

$mv = mv_{1} + mv_{1}$

$V_{1}=\frac{V}{2}$


[IMG]


And from energy conservation 

$\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}=\left (\frac{1}{2}\times m\left (\frac{V}{2}\right )^{2}\right )\times 2+\frac{1}{2}Kx^{2}$

$\frac{mv^{2}}{2}-\frac{mv^{2}}{4}=\frac{1}{2}kx^{2}$

$\frac{mv^{2}}{4}=\frac{1}{2}kx^{2}$

Then the maximum compression in the spring is 

$x=\sqrt{\frac{mv^{2}}{2K}}$

$\Rightarrow$ x = $v\sqrt{\frac{m}{2K}}$

text:
A boy of mass 4 kg is standing on a piece of wood having mass 5 kg. If the coefficient of friction between the wood and the floor is 0.5, the maximum force that the boy can exert on the rope so that the piece of wood does not move from its place is $__________ N. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer) [Take $g = 10 ms^{-2}$ ]


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
No angle is given for the rope held by the boy, so that segment is taken as vertical; the other end of the same rope pulls the wood horizontally, and the tension throughout equals the force $T$ exerted by the boy.

For the boy and wood together, the rope pulls up with $T$ at the boy's hands, so the normal reaction of the floor is

$N=(4+5)\times 10-T=90-T$

The wood stays at rest as long as the horizontal pull $T$ does not exceed limiting friction:

$T\leq μN=0.5(90-T)\Rightarrow 1.5T\leq 45\Rightarrow T\leq 30\text{N}$

Hence, the answer is 30.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift

text: A body of mass 1 kg rests on a horizontal floor with which it has a coefficient of static friction $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. It is desired to make the body move by applying the minimum possible force F N. The value of F will be $____________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer) [Take $g = 10 ms^{-2}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the force $F$ act at an angle $θ$ above the horizontal. The normal reaction is $N=mg-F\sin θ$, and the body is on the verge of moving when

$F\cos θ=μ(mg-F\sin θ)\Rightarrow F=\dfrac{μmg}{\cos θ+μ\sin θ}$

$F$ is least when $\cos θ+μ\sin θ$ is greatest. Its maximum value is $\sqrt{1+μ^{2}}$, reached at $\tan θ=μ=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, that is $θ=30^{\circ }$.

$F_{\min }=\dfrac{μmg}{\sqrt{1+μ^{2}}}=\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\times 1\times 10}{\sqrt{1+\dfrac{1}{3}}}=\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{3}}\times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=5\text{N}$

A horizontal push would need $μmg=\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{3}}\approx 5.77\text{N}$, which is larger: pulling at $30^{\circ }$ reduces the normal reaction and hence the friction.

Hence, the answer is 5.

text:
A particle of mass m moves in a circular orbit in a 
central potential field $U(r) = U_{0}r^{4}$. If Bohr's quantization conditions 
are applied, radii of possible 
orbitals $r_{n}$ vary with $n^{\frac{1}{α}}$, where $α$ is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{F}=-\frac{d\vec{u}}{dr}$

$=-\frac{d}{dr}(U_{0}r^{4})$

$\vec{F}=-4U_{0}r^{3}$

$\because$ $\frac{mv^{2}}{r}=4U_{0}r^{3}$

$mv^{2}=4U_{0}r^{4}$

Then $v\propto r^{2}$

$\because$ $mvr=\frac{nh}{2π}$

Then $r^{3}\propto \qquad n$

$r~\propto (n)^{\frac{1}{3}}$

So the value of $α=3$

text: Seawater at a frequency f = 9 $\times$ $10^{2} Hz$, has permittivity $ε$ = 80$ε_{0}$ and resistivity $ρ$ = 0.25 $\Omega$m. Imagine a parallel plate capacitor is immersed in seawater and is driven by an alternating voltage source $V(t) = V_{0} \sin (2π$ft). Then the conduction current density becomes $10^{x}$ times the displacement current density after time t = $\frac{1}{800}$s. The value of x is $_____________. ($Given : $\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}=9\times 10^{9}$ $Nm^{2}C^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Between the plates the seawater carries a conduction current density $J_{c}=\dfrac{E}{ρ}$ and a displacement current density $J_{d}=ε\dfrac{dE}{dt}$, where $E=\dfrac{V_{0}\sin (2πft)}{d}$ for plate separation $d$.

$J_{c}=\dfrac{V_{0}\sin (2πft)}{ρd},J_{d}=\dfrac{εV_{0}(2πf)\cos (2πft)}{d}$

$\dfrac{J_{c}}{J_{d}}=\dfrac{\tan (2πft)}{2πfερ}$

At $t=\dfrac{1}{800}\text{s}$: $2πft=2π\times 900\times \dfrac{1}{800}=\dfrac{9π}{4}$, so $\tan (2πft)=\tan \dfrac{π}{4}=1$.

With $ε=80ε_{0}=\dfrac{80}{4π\times 9\times 10^{9}}\text{F m}^{-1}$:

$2πfερ=2π\times 900\times \dfrac{80}{4π\times 9\times 10^{9}}\times 0.25=\dfrac{900\times 80\times 0.25}{2\times 9\times 10^{9}}=10^{-6}$

$\dfrac{J_{c}}{J_{d}}=\dfrac{1}{10^{-6}}=10^{6}\Rightarrow x=6$

Hence, the answer is 6.
